title: Questions 155-157 refer to the following article.
passage_1:
(Singapore)—The price of long-grain rice has climbed steeply in recent months because of severe weather disrupting major leading exporters. Dr. Amara Lindqvist, an agricultural specialist, explained, “Prolonged flooding in Vietnam and an unexpected dry season in Thailand have substantially reduced crop yields this year. In fact, this combination of climate-related events is infrequent but extremely damaging.” – [1] –.

These environmental conditions have produced a shortage of rice on international markets. As a result, food processors that depend on supplies from those countries are facing challenges in securing adequate inventory to satisfy consumer demand. – [2] –. They have approached other rice-producing countries, such as India and Cambodia, in the hope that growers there can supply the required quantities. – [3] –. The majority of the goods being produced are already reserved for current customers. – [4] –.
